notes: 2nd Marines landed in the Tulagi group on 7 August 1942 as part of the northern attack, under Vandegrift’s landing force (Miller, ch. III; Zimmerman, ch. II). The regiment later served on Guadalcanal; a date for that move was not entered in this increment. Confidence 0.7 for the Tulagi landing.

location_qualifier: about 2,000 yards west of Point Cruz
source_locator: R2225: ch. VIII, Kokumbona Offensive, 1-4 November
current_activity: advancing about 2,000 yards west of Point Cruz before being halted
notes: Miller, ch. VIII: the two battalions of the 2nd Marines (brought from Tulagi, 3rd Battalion sent there to rest) passed the 5th Marines on 2 November. On 3 November 1st Battalion, 2nd Marines, and the Whaling Group led the assault, Colonel Arthur taking over from Edson after the pocket was reduced. On 4 November the 2nd Marines (less 3rd Battalion) and 1st Battalion, 164th Infantry, reached a point about 2,000 yards west of Point Cruz, then dug in when division halted the advance because of the Koli landing. Confidence 0.5: Miller only in this increment.

notes: Miller, ch. VIII: the 2nd and 8th Marines recrossed the Matanikau on 11 November, covered by 1st Battalion, 164th Infantry, after the mid-November convoy warning. Confidence 0.5: Miller only in this increment.

notes: Miller, chapter IX, and Hough, Ludwig and Shaw, Part VI, chapter 9, date the landing of 2nd Marine Division headquarters and the 6th Marines to 4 January 1943. The 2nd Marines were already on the island (Tulagi, 7 August) and are treated from this day as under that headquarters. Confidence 0.7.
